newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end lower on Taiwan, crush pace.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end lower on Taiwan, crush pace.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended lower on Friday, pressured by news Taiwan had passed on several soybean tenders overnight and by a lower than expected crush, traders said.

"The trade realized this Taiwan foot and mouth disease was probably a bigger issue than was believed yesterday," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities. "When we saw tenders passed overnight, that was the wake-up call."
Taiwan overnight passed on a tender for 54,000 tonnes South American soybeans and a joint U.S. corn/soybean tender. The moves came after Taiwan announced a pork export ban.

Traders in Taiwan attributed the moves to a cutback in feed demand following a cut in Taiwan's herd due to the disease outbreak. Taiwanese buyers said this year's corn imports could fall by 20 percent as a result of the export ban. Soybean and meal imports were also seen declining.
Soybeans closed 15 to five cents per bushel lower with May off 9-1/2 at $8.42-1/2. New crop November closed down 5-1/4 at $7.12-3/4.
NOPA's weekly crush figure of 28.12 million bushels was below trade expectations for 28.5 million to 29.5 million bushels and also weighed on the nearbys.

"When the crush came out at the low end of expectation, that set the tone for the overnight (Project A trade)," Roose said. "There was pretty good cash movement and the basis came under pressure. On top of that, the basis yesterday afternoon and this morning in South America was under pressure."
New crop months escaped the brunt of the sell-off, boosted by bear spreads, floor sources said. Traders speculated the spreads were tied to Taiwan's pork export ban.

"We're seeing some bear spreading as a result of this Taiwan news," a trader said. "We will have increased feed demand in the U.S. but it won't show up until the new crop months. Pork producers will increase herds but they can't do it overnight."
Chartists said a close above $8.40 in the May contract confirmed the long-term bullish trend was in place. The market closed above the four- and 20-day moving averages.
Support was pegged at $8.35-1/4 in the May with resistance at $8.47-3/4.

On the day, funds sold at least 10 million bushels with Refco Inc a seller of four million May, traders said. ADM sold 3.5 million May and Prudential Securities and SAK Futures each sold two million May.
In options, CIS sold 400 May $8.00 calls at 50 cents and another 400 May $8.25 calls at 31 to 32 cents.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 68,000 contracts, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 86,654 contracts.
